---
title: "Explore the data"
subtitle: "Pre-rendered views of the hub, switchable by view and outcome domain"
toc: false
---

Pick a view and, for effect-size views, an outcome domain. Each combination is a static figure generated by the pipeline, so what you see is fixed to the data version this site was built from. The selection is kept in the page address, so a view can be linked to.

```{=html}
<div class="mf-viz" data-manifest="generated/viz/manifest.json">
  <div class="mf-viz-controls">
    <label for="viz-view">View
      <select id="viz-view"></select>
    </label>
    <label for="viz-domain">Outcome domain
      <select id="viz-domain"></select>
    </label>
  </div>
  <p class="mf-viz-desc" aria-live="polite"></p>
  <div class="mf-viz-plot" aria-live="polite">
    <p class="mf-viz-status">Loading…</p>
  </div>
  <p class="mf-viz-actions"><a class="mf-viz-open" href="#" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Open this figure as SVG</a></p>
</div>
```

::: {.mf-band}
**Reading the plots.** Effect sizes are standardized mean changes from baseline to post-intervention in training arms (non-training controls are excluded). Point size reflects precision. In effect-size views for a single domain, colour separates high-load from low-load arms. Across all domains, colour and marker shape both identify the domain. See [Analyses](analyses.qmd) for how the effect sizes are computed.
:::
